title: Compliance Administrator- Leading Recruitment Company
description:
Join Prospero Teaching - Where Passion Meets Purpose in Education!

For over 20 years, Prospero Teaching has been a trusted leader in connecting teaching and support staff with schools, academies, and nurseries across the UK and internationally. We proudly offer our services to a broad range of educational settings, including EYFS, Primary, Secondary, Further Education, SEN, and PRUs.

About the Role

As a Compliance Administrator, you will be a key member of our compliance team, responsible for ensuring candidates meet the necessary regulatory and internal requirements to work within the education sector. You will play a vital role in maintaining compliance with industry standards and fostering a smooth recruitment process for candidates.

Key Responsibilities
- Collaborate with the compliance team to ensure candidates meet all compliance standards for the education sector.
- Follow established operational processes and procedures to ensure adherence to regulations and industry standards.
- Guide and support candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Conduct compliance checks, including but not limited to right-to-work, DBS, reference, and employment history verifications.
- Maintain and update accurate candidate records.
- Organise and verify candidate documentation.
- Respond to both internal and external inquiries efficiently and professionally.

About You

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented individual with:
- A good general education (minimum GCSEs in Maths and English, grades A-C, or equivalent).
- Strong relationship-building skills.
- The ability to work effectively under deadlines.
- Excellent administrative and organizational abilities, with a talent for prioritizing tasks.
- Strong communication and customer service skills.
- An understanding of confidentiality and data protection.
- A proactive problem-solving mindset.
- A commitment to safeguarding practices.

Benefits
- Competitive salary with a commission structure.
- Ongoing training and opportunities for professional development.
- Clear career advancement prospects within the company.
- A dynamic and collaborative work environment.
- Private healthcare.
- Quarterly performance-based incentives.

Join us and be part of a team that's helping drive one of the UK's fastest-growing recruitment firms forward.

title: HR and Compliance Administrator
description:
We are seeking a highly organised and detail-oriented HR and Compliance Administrator to support both the HR and Compliance functions of the business. This varied role will involve coordinating the employee lifecycle from onboarding through to leavers, maintaining accurate HR records, supporting payroll administration, and ensuring compliance with internal procedures and external funding and audit requirements.

This position would suit an experienced administrator with excellent attention to detail and strong organisational skills. Previous HR administration experience would be advantageous but is not essential, as full training can be provided for the right individual.

Leeds City Centre (LS1), 28,000 per annum, Monday to Friday, 8:30am - 5:00pm

This is a fully office-based position.

Key Responsibilities
HR Administration
- Coordinate the onboarding process for new employees, ensuring all documentation is completed accurately and within required timescales.
- Process employment references and right to work documentation.
- Arrange and monitor DBS checks where required.
- Prepare contracts of employment, contract amendments and change of terms documentation.
- Administer probation review processes and maintain accurate employee records.
- Process employee leavers and ensure all relevant documentation is completed.
- Collate payroll information including starters, leavers, contractual changes, sickness, holiday and payroll amendments for submission within deadlines.
- Maintain confidential employee files and HR databases, ensuring compliance with GDPR.
- Provide day-to-day administrative support to the HR team.

Compliance and Administration
- Validate documentation and records to ensure compliance with internal procedures and external funding requirements.
- Perform eligibility and compliance checks where required.
- Accurately enter and maintain information on internal management information systems.
- Create and maintain tracking spreadsheets, databases and compliance records.
- Prepare documentation and records for audits, inspections and quality assurance processes.
- Carry out regular compliance audits and identify any discrepancies or missing documentation.
- Register learners or employees on relevant external systems where applicable and ensure all deadlines are met.
- Maintain procedures, templates and administrative documentation.
- Support external audits, inspections and verification visits, ensuring documentation is accurate and readily available.
- Ensure compliance with organisational policies, procedures and regulatory requirements.
- Assist with continuous improvement of administrative and compliance processes.
- Undertake any other administrative duties required to support the wider business.

Knowledge, Skills and Experience
Essential
- Minimum of two years' experience within an administrative or compliance-based role.
- Excellent organisational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to prioritise workload and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
- Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.
- Strong IT skills including Microsoft Office 365, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- Experience maintaining confidential records with a high level of accuracy.
- GCSE Grade 4/C or above (or equivalent) in English and Maths.

Desirable
- Previous HR administration experience including onboarding, contracts and payroll administration.
- Experience arranging DBS checks and maintaining personnel records.
- Experience working within a regulated or compliance-driven environment.
- Knowledge of audit processes and quality assurance requirements.
- Experience using HR or management information systems.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

Personal Attributes
- Highly organised and methodical.
- Professional with excellent attention to detail.
- Able to maintain confidentiality at all times.
- Positive, proactive and willing to support colleagues.
- Strong team player with the ability to build effective working relationships.
- Flexible approach with a willingness to learn new systems and processes.

What We're Looking For

This role would suit someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced administrative environment where accuracy and organisation are essential. Whether your background is in HR administration, compliance, education administration or general business support, you'll be someone who takes pride in producing high-quality work, enjoys working with processes and systems, and is committed to maintaining high standards of compliance across the business.

Huntress Search Ltd acts as a Recruitment Agency in relation to all Permanent roles and as a Recruitment Business in relation to all Temporary roles.

We practice a diverse and inclusive recruitment process that ensures equal opportunity for all we work with, irrespective of race, sexual orientation, mental or physical disability, age or gender. As an organisation, we encourage applications from all backgrounds and will ensure measures are met when required, to allow a fair process throughout.

PLEASE NOTE: We can only consider applications from candidates who have the right to work in the UK.

title: HR Coordinator
description:
HR Coordinator

Salary £27,051 - £28,599 per annum

Hours: 37 per week

Our team is growing! An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated and proactive HR Coordinator to join our friendly and supportive HR team at Leeds College of Building. You ll play a key role in supporting the College s people function, with a particular focus on the recruitment and onboarding of staff. Working collaboratively within the team, you ll help deliver an exceptional employee experience and contribute to the successful delivery of our People Strategy.

This is an exciting time to join the College, recently recognised as a Construction Technical Excellence College for Yorkshire and the Humber region, with ambitious plans for further expansion and development. If you re passionate about people, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and want to be part of a college that is shaping the future of education in Construction and the Built Environment, we d love to hear from you.

You must have the ability to work to deadlines, a high level of accuracy & attention to detail and be able to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders. Additionally, you should possess at least a Level 2 qualification or equivalent.

In return, we offer a warm and welcoming college with an excellent benefits package that includes:
- A 25-day annual leave entitlement, plus 8 Bank Holidays and 10 college closure days, including Christmas (plus an additional 5 days of leave after 5 years of service with us)
- Family-friendly policies, including flexible working arrangements
- A well-respected pension scheme (West Yorkshire Pension Fund with an above average employer contribution)
- Free car parking at all our college sites (on a first come, first served basis)
- Family friendly policies and opportunities for flexible working
- Superb opportunities for training and development
- Discounted travel on public transport and a Cycle to work scheme
- Discounts and offers at major Street and Online retailers
- Access to an Employee Assistance Programme.

So, if you d like to be part of a unique organisation that supports one of the largest and most diverse employment sectors in the UK, we d love to hear from you.

Please note that all applications should be completed online. Please visit the vacancies section of our website or press APPLY.

Closing date for applications: 28th October 2026

The College reserves the right to close this vacancy early if a sufficient number of applications are received. We therefore encourage early applications.

Please note this position is subject to an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check and in line with KCSIE (2026) an online check will be conducted on information available in the public domain.

Leeds College of Building is committed to safeguarding children, young people and vulnerable adults. It is also committed to the Prevent programme and the requirement to prevent people being drawn into terrorism and expects all staff to share these commitments.

Leeds College of Building is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse community. We value the unique perspectives and experiences of individuals from all backgrounds and actively encourage applications from individuals from an ethnic minority and the LGBTQIA+ community, as they are under-represented at our College. Join us in creating a workplace where everyone can thrive to provide the best construction and the built environment education in England.

title: Recruitment Resourcer
description:
Recruitment Resourcer
Aqumen Recruitment

Salary: £26,000 per annum
Location: Carrwood Park, Selby Road, Leeds, LS15 4 LG
Contract: Full-time, permanent
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9.00am 5.30pm

Aqumen Recruitment is looking for an organised, enthusiastic Recruitment Resourcer to support our temporary, permanent and event recruitment teams.

Reporting to the Operations Director, you ll help with day-to-day recruitment activity, maintain accurate candidate records and ensure candidates are interviewed and fully briefed on job opportunities.

Your main duties will include:
- Supporting recruitment across our temporary, permanent and event recruitment teams.
- Accurately updating our CRM, ensuring candidate information and recruitment activity are recorded correctly.
- Interviewing candidates to understand their skills, experience, availability and suitability for roles.
- Briefing candidates on job roles, including duties, working hours, location and expectations.
- Maintaining clear, professional communication with candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Following company procedures for candidate registration, right-to-work checks, confidentiality and data protection.

We re looking for someone who:
- Communicates clearly and confidently with candidates and colleagues.
- Is organised, pays close attention to detail and maintains accurate records.
- Is comfortable using computer systems and learning new platforms.
- Can manage competing priorities and work across different recruitment teams.
- Is keen to learn and handles confidential information professionally.
- Preferably have a Driving License and a car.

In return, we offer:
- 25 days annual leave plus statutory holidays.
- Training and development, including access to the Savage Recruitment Academy, coaching from experienced colleagues and training from external providers.
- Practical training in our CRM, candidate registration, right-to-work processes, GDPR and other relevant platforms.
- A NEST workplace pension.
- A company laptop and mobile phone for work use.
- An Employee Assistance Programme.
- Reimbursement for hearing and eye tests against valid receipts.
- Reimbursement of eligible business expenses and mileage in line with company policy.

Our current informal working arrangement allows homeworking on Wednesdays and Fridays, subject to business needs and attendance at the office when required.

Our office at Carrwood Park is set within 100 acres of Yorkshire countryside. Employees can enjoy events throughout the year, including summer picnics by the lake, pizza parties and a bonfire and fireworks display that family members can attend free of charge.

If you enjoy working with people, keeping things organised and helping candidates prepare for their next role, we d like to hear from you.

To apply: Send your CV

Appointment is subject to verification of your right to work in the UK.
